subject: Re: Novus Health — eastus2 degradation / hotpatch + cross-region cutover request
messages:
From: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@novushealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@novushealth.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent — eastus2 latency + 5xx surge (Novus Health)

Rachel —

We started seeing a large increase in 5xx rates and p95 latency from ~07:45 PT across our user-facing endpoints backed by eastus2. App metrics show request queueing on your side; errors are correlated with token-generation timeouts. This is impacting real-time clinician workflows.

What we can confirm:
- Error spike started ~07:42 PT, peaked ~08:00 PT (5xx rate ~12% on our traffic).
- Affected model: open-llama-v2-13b (pinned in our integration).
- Mitigation attempts on our side: client retries and reduced concurrency — limited effect.

We need immediate help to keep traffic moving. Can you confirm a plan for a hotpatch or traffic failover to a healthy region? If cutover is required, we need timing, expected RTO, and a commitment on token-loss/consistency. Also flagging that we will need a short executive summary for our CTO and for procurement (this is impacting a high-touch contract).

Attachments: incident-snippets attached (novus_incident_log_20270620.csv).

—Samuel Ortiz
Director, Platform Engineering
Novus Health
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@novushealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 08:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent — eastus2 latency + 5xx surge (Novus Health)

Samuel — thanks for the quick signal and the logs. I’m escalating immediately and copying our on-call infra and cloud ops. Short answers up front: we will execute a coordinated cross-region rehome to westus2 as the mitigatory step, and we’re preparing an executive note for your CTO.

Planned immediate actions (call to action):
1) David — please confirm plan and ETA for staged cutover (prefix pin / traffic steering) and whether we need a short rolling hotpatch to the model variant.
2) Laura — please prepare the failover playbook artifacts and an ask for capacity borrow/priority pin if westus2 needs reserved QPS.
3) Samuel — we will aim for a ~20–30 minute controlled reroute after readiness confirmation; during the cutover we expect a small percentage of in-flight requests to fail (we will capture and forward logs).

I will update Novus’s execs with timeline and rationale. Samuel, can you share the name/email of your CTO so I can close the loop?

Attachments: playbook_crossregion_cutover.pdf (internal runbook).

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Head of Customer Success, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@novushealth.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novus eastus2 — proposed cross-region rehome to westus2

Rachel / Samuel / Laura —

On the infra side: we’ve validated telemetry and see sustained queueing at the serving layer in eastus2 for the pinned model at the tokenization stage. Initial hypothesis: a degraded kernel instance set combined with an overloaded kvcache population during a concurrent high-similarity prefix load.

Immediate technical plan (step-by-step):
- Step 0 (ongoing): snapshot current kvcache metrics, scale read replicas for perf counters.
- Step 1 (T+10 min after approval): open westus2 ingress, verify model variant availability and KV warmup on a dark-canary slice (1% traffic).
- Step 2 (T+20 min): shift non-critical shards (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with circuit breakers and request-level retries disabled at client to avoid amplification. We’ll keep TTLs on cache to avoid cold-start thrash.
- Step 3: run smoke tests, monitor end-to-end p95 and 5xx; rollback immediately on error spike.

Expected impact: 15–30 minute window for full rehome; estimate transient failure rate affecting ~0.5–2% of in-flight requests depending on concurrency patterns. We will stream logs to the same shared bucket and produce a postmortem slice for Novus.

Operational asks:
- Exec approval to borrow westus2 priority capacity for 2 hours (we’ll release when stable).
- Approval to temporarily pin a higher-performance quantized variant if required (this may change token-level cost).

I’ll start the dark-canary prep now; will report readiness in ~8–12 minutes.

—David Kim
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@novushealth.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Novus Health — executive approval request for cross-region failover and temporary capacity pin

Hi Marissa —

Bringing this to you for quick exec authorization. Customer: Novus Health (Strategic enterprise, deal NOVUS-ENT-2026-Q4). They are experiencing a regional degradation in eastus2 (increased p95 and 5xx spike impacting clinician-facing flows). We propose a controlled cross-region rehome to westus2 plus a temporary priority capacity borrow (2 hours) and, if required, an emergency pin of a higher-perf quantized model variant.

Why we need a fast decision:
- Customer SLA exposure and potential contractual impact if clinicians can’t complete workflows.
- We will need to commit to an RTO (~20–30m) and communicate expected transient failures.

Risk/Cost tradeoffs:
- Borrowing westus2 priority capacity is feasible; estimated additional cost for 2 hours: ~$4.2k (chargeback or one-time credit discussion).
- Pinning a higher-performance variant may increase per-token cost ~15–25% during the window.
- Rehome mitigates continued user impact but carries a small risk of in-flight request loss (~0.5–2%).

Requested approvals (please reply-all):
1) Exec approval to borrow westus2 priority capacity for up to 2 hours.
2) Approval to temporarily pin a higher-perf quantized model variant if required.
3) Authorization to issue a one-time service credit if the post-incident review recommends it.

If we get a quick thumbs-up from Marissa, David will execute the staged cutover and Laura will coordinate the customer comms. I’ll draft the executive note for Novus’s CTO once we have ETA.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Head of Customer Success, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
